title: Closed-loop environment replay harness for customer-specific on-prem topologies
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Build a deterministic, closed-loop replay harness that can reproduce customer on-prem/VPC topologies and traffic mixes for repeatable performance benchmarking. The harness must support: 1) ingesting environment snapshots (network topology, node resource profiles, model variants, and autoscaler state), 2) deterministic request replay with configurable seedable RNG for prompt selection and inter-arrival timings, 3) mixed synthetic+production traffic blending to emulate real token distribution, and 4) automated metric collection for tokens/sec, p95 latency, p99 tail, error rates, and KV cache warmup curves. This ticket focuses on the harness core, reproducibility guarantees, and regression detection plumbing (baseline storage, diffing, alerting).
acceptance_criteria: Can ingest an environment snapshot tarball and materialize a reproducible test cluster in the private harness runner
Replayed runs produce deterministic latency and throughput curves when RNG seed and snapshot are fixed (within documented nondeterminism bounds)
Metrics emitted to the benchmarking metrics namespace include tokens_per_second, p95_latency_ms, p99_latency_ms, tail_error_rate, and kv_cache_hit_rate
Automated regression detection flags runs whose p95 increases by >10% against the pinned baseline and creates a Linear regression alert with artifacts
CLI and YAML config allow: workload composition (prod-sampled ratio), sequence length distribution, client-side KV cache warmup policy, and concurrency profile
Store run artifacts (traces, token histograms, raw request logs, runner config) to S3/GCS with stable naming for later replay
tasks: Design environment snapshot schema and validator (network, nodes, runtime flags, model pins)
Implement deterministic request player with pluggable scheduling backends (sync, poisson, recorded-interarrival)
Integrate metrics exporter and ensure Prometheus-compatible labels and histogram buckets
Add baseline store and compare job that runs after each replay and writes a regression decision artifact
Create e2e test that replays a saved customer run and asserts metric stability within bounds
progress_updates: 2026-02-18: Kickoff meeting with Solutions and Infra; agreed snapshot must include autoscaler and GPU topology metadata
2026-02-25: Prototype deterministic player implemented (seeded prompt sampler + fixed inter-arrival); validated on small on-prem lab cluster
2026-03-03: Spike showed KV cache warmup introduces nondeterminism for early tokens; decided to add warmup phase and report hot-start vs cold-start metrics separately
2026-03-09: Integrated OpenTelemetry traces from the runtime to correlate p95 spikes with kernel selection changes; added trace_id tagging for each replay iteration

2026-03-12: Baseline store design reviewed by PM and Research; using S3 path + run-id + sha256(config) to identify baselines. Regression rule threshold default set to 10% p95 increase or 5% tokens/sec drop
review_feedback: PM (Elena Rodriguez): emphasize customer reproducibility guarantees and include guidance for acceptable nondeterminism in PRD
Research (Tom Beck): request to capture sequence-length histograms and per-model kv hit rate for deeper regression root-cause analysis
Security (Priya Shah): require that snapshots exclude customer PII and that snapshot ingestion has an allowlist for buckets and object paths
regression_detection_plan: After each run compute delta versus pinned baseline for: p95, p99, tokens_per_second, tail_error_rate, kv_cache_hit_rate
Regression job writes an artifact with summary.json and diff.svg to the run S3 folder and opens a Linear regression issue when thresholds are breached
Attach trace ids and the top 5 slowest spans to the regression issue to accelerate RCA
Support manual overrides for noisy baselines and allow marking a run as the new baseline via the CLI
run_history: 2026-02-26: Lab run A (snapshot lab-v1) - tokens/sec 1.8k, p95 82ms, kv_hit 0.12 - used to validate deterministic player
2026-03-05: Customer-mimic run B (snapshot cust-42) - tokens/sec 2.1k, p95 110ms, observed early p95 spikes during model swap. Traces linked in artifacts
2026-03-11: Warmup policy iteration - cold-start p95 normalized by adding 30s KV warmup; p95 variance reduced from 22% to 7% between runs
notes: Decisions: warmup phase will be configurable and reported separately (cold vs warm metrics)
Trade-offs: full fidelity replay (network jitter, kernel scheduling) is costly; we will document fidelity tiers (fast, realistic, full)
Follow-ups: integrate with Console rollouts to run replay harness automatically after canary->prod promotion
Next steps: implement baseline compare job, add secure snapshot ingestion, and run customer reproducibility audit with Solutions team
